subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class cron-scoped tool policy, make cron inherit subagent policy, or keep per-job `payload.toolsAllow` as the only hard cron tool boundary?
rationale: The choice defines a public config surface and scheduled-automation security boundary, including whether existing announce jobs keep direct `message` access by default.

options.title: Add cron-scoped policy
options.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` or an equivalent typed cron policy with explicit precedence, docs, config metadata, migration/default behavior, and tests for announce/message behavior.

options.title: Inherit subagent policy
options.body: Treat isolated cron sessions as policy peers of subagents so `tools.subagents.tools` applies to cron, accepting the coupling and documenting the shared behavior.

options.title: Keep per-job only
options.body: Decline a global cron config surface and document that operators must use per-job `payload.toolsAllow` or runtime/prompt safeguards for cron restrictions.

recommendation.title: Add cron-scoped policy
recommendation.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` or an equivalent typed cron policy with explicit precedence, docs, config metadata, migration/default behavior, and tests for announce/message behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across cron/session/capability-profile work and prior issue review context.
